# DSH Studio v0.9.10

## Changes and security

- Add a collapsible workbench sidebar with direct access to recent sessions, tools, settings, and profiles.
- Match the desktop chat design tokens with a restrained neutral palette and an OpenAI Sans-first system UI font stack using the original 510/590 interface weights. Use a 46 px title bar, center the view selector, give the expanded sidebar a 275 px width, and use 40 px primary navigation rows. The managed Harness integration synchronizes semantic theme colors while accepting only the expected parent-window message shape.
- Keep Harness's own conversation sidebar in chat mode, avoiding duplicate navigation.

## Fixes and polish

- Reflow the console into runtime controls above a full-width log, with a single-column layout at narrow content widths.
- Focus session search when opened from the sidebar, including from a session reader or another tab.
- Update screenshot fixtures for current native contracts and lazy-loaded panes.
- Pin the Cordis core and plugin compatibility floors declared by each selected Harness release, preventing npm dependency drift from terminating older runtimes after readiness. Probe the real document and preserve Harness output when startup fails.

## Installation and limitations

- Upgrade in place or use the in-app updater. Full includes offline dependencies; Lite downloads them when needed.
- This release follows the layout and typography of desktop chat applications without bundling OpenAI font files. Harness's composer and branding remain upstream-owned; this is not a pixel-for-pixel clone.

## Verification

- Local frontend build, lint, 269 frontend tests, 53 packaging script tests, Rust workspace tests, and public-contract checks passed.
- Browser checks covered light and dark themes, the 900×620 minimum window, expanded and collapsed navigation, title-bar overlap, recent sessions, search focus, and Harness theme-token overrides. Isolated cold installs and real Profile boots passed for `0.1.1-rc.1` and `0.1.2-rc.1`; the release workflow validates native packages on all three platforms.
